evidence.claim: US citizens (and other visa-exempt nationals) may stay in the Schengen area, which includes Portugal, up to 90 days in any 180-day period without a visa; passport must be valid at least 3 months beyond the intended departure date and have been issued within the last 10 years.

ETIAS (the EU's pre-travel authorisation for visa-exempt visitors) is not yet operational or required as of Aug 2026. The EU quietly removed its previously-stated Q4 2026 launch target from the official ETIAS site in Jul 2026; 2027 is the most-likely next launch window per immigration-law commentary, but no confirmed date has been announced — genuinely unresolved as of this research.
Portugal uses the euro; ATMs and major cards (Visa, Amex, Mastercard/Maestro, JCB, Diners) are widely accepted; tipping ~5–10% in restaurants/taxis is customary but not mandatory.

Portuguese consumer law (Lei n.º 24/96, Art. 9 §4) says a consumer is not obliged to pay for any good or service — including the bread/olives 'couvert' automatically brought to the table — that was not previously and expressly ordered; a diner may decline it at no charge. Restaurants must display the couvert price and can face ASAE fines for charging it without disclosure.
Portugal's national emergency number is 112 (police/fire/ambulance, free, 24/7); SNS 24 health line is 808 24 24 24.

The EU's 'Roam Like at Home' rules only cover EU/EEA (plus Moldova/Ukraine) residents on an EU-based plan — a US traveler's home phone plan is NOT covered by these rules and roaming can be expensive without a specific international plan, local SIM, or eSIM.

Lisbon Airport (LIS) to city center: Metro red line (Aeroporto–Saldanha), roughly 20 min; Metro single fare €1.92 by contactless bank card or €1.72 on a prepaid Navegante 'zapping' card; taxi/rideshare roughly €10–15 including luggage fee.
Metro Lisboa single fare €1.92 (card) / €1.72 (Navegante zapping); operates 06:30–01:00 daily; a Navegante card costs €0.50 once.

The Aerobus airport shuttle service was permanently discontinued in 2022 and no longer operates, despite still appearing as bookable on several third-party booking sites. The official Lisbon Airport transport page lists Metro/Carris buses/Flixbus/taxi and makes no mention of Aerobus; aerobus.pt itself 404s.

Lisbon–Porto Alfa Pendular fare and exact journey time could NOT be confirmed against the operator's own site: cp.pt is a JS-rendered SPA that returns only page headers with no fare content to automated fetch (attempted on 4 different cp.pt URLs including a PDF tariff sheet). Aggregator estimates (unconfirmed) put standard 2nd class around €25–34, 1st class around €48, journey ≈2h45m, with promotional fares from ≈€9.50–7.50 on advance/promo purchase.

CP's Sintra line (Rossio ↔ Sintra) runs roughly every 15–20 min at peak, journey ≈40 min, integrated into the Navegante fare system — but exact current fare/frequency could not be confirmed against cp.pt directly (same JS-rendering block as the Alfa Pendular page).

Scotturb is the official transport operator for the Sintra palace shuttle buses (434 'Circuito da Pena', 435 to Monserrate); its own homepage confirms this role, but the route-specific fare/frequency subpages 404'd on every attempt — treat any specific fare figure as unconfirmed pending a direct re-check.
A 24-hour transport pass covering Scotturb bus lines 434 and 435 costs €10.96, sold directly on Parques de Sintra's own ticketing platform — transport only, monument tickets sold separately.

The bus route to Cabo da Roca commonly cited in older guides as 'Scotturb 403' was discontinued/renumbered when Carris Metropolitana took over the route in Jan 2023 — the current route is Carris Metropolitana line 1253. Any source still citing 'Scotturb 403' is stale.

Portugal's mandatory national public holidays (Código do Trabalho Art. 234): Jan 1, Good Friday, Easter Sunday, Apr 25, May 1, Corpus Christi, Jun 10, Aug 15, Oct 5, Nov 1, Dec 1, Dec 8, Dec 25. For 2027, Good Friday falls Mar 26 and Easter Sunday Mar 28 — both before the Apr 10–19, 2027 trip window; Freedom Day (Apr 25) falls 6 days after the trip ends. No national holiday falls inside the trip window. Lisbon's Santo António (Jun 13) and Porto's São João (Jun 24) municipal holidays also fall well outside the window.
Open daily 08:00–21:00 (extended to 22:00 Jul 1–Sep 30; shortened to 19:00 on Dec 24/25/31/Jan 1); walk-in only, no reservation system; ≈€1.50–1.60 per tart, ≈€9 for a box of 6.

Pastéis de Belém draws real queues and heavy foot traffic, but the line visible outside is almost always for takeaway only — walking in through the main entrance reaches a 1,000+ seat dine-in room most visitors never realize exists, with a table usually available in under 10 minutes even at peak times. Quietest before 09:00 on weekdays or after 18:00 any day; peak congestion is 10:00–17:00, especially weekends Apr–Oct.

Quietest before 09:00 on weekdays or after 18:00 any day; peak congestion is 10:00–17:00, especially weekends Apr–Oct.

Manteigaria has 13 Lisbon locations (incl. Chiado, Time Out Market, Belém, Rossio) and 4 Porto locations (Bolhão, Clérigos, Santa Catarina, Largo São Domingos) — a genuine multi-city alternative to Pastéis de Belém, though itself now a large chain (also in Paris, Madrid, Hong Kong). Price ≈€1.20–1.30/tart (aggregator-sourced, not confirmed on the official site).

Time Out Market Lisboa: Sun–Wed 10:00–24:00, Thu–Sat 10:00–02:00, in the historic Mercado da Ribeira building, 26 stalls + 8 bars. The operator's own page describes it as 'one of Portugal's most popular tourist attractions,' welcoming thousands of visitors daily.

Market stalls Mon–Fri 08:00–20:00, Sat 08:00–18:00, closed Sun/holidays; in-market restaurants Mon–Sat 08:00–24:00, closed Sun/holidays. Reopened after a multi-year renovation (aggregator-sourced reopening date of 2026-09-15 — not independently confirmed via an official/press fetch); page shows normal operations with no closure notices.
Café Santiago (francesinha, since 1959): Mon–Sat 12:00–22:45, closed Sunday. Price not listed on the official page (aggregator estimate ≈€8.50–10, unconfirmed).
Typical Portuguese meal windows: breakfast 07:30–10:00, lunch (main meal) 12:00–14:30, afternoon snack ~17:00, dinner 19:30–22:30 — noticeably later than typical US dinner hours.
Tue–Sun 09:30–17:30, closed Mondays (and Jan 1, Easter Sunday, May 1, Jun 13, Dec 25); adult admission €15.

Cloister Tue–Sun 09:30–17:30 (last entry 17:00); Church Tue–Sat 10:30–17:00, Sun/holidays 14:00–17:00; closed Mondays (and Jan 1, Easter Sunday, May 1, Jun 13, Dec 25). Adult admission €18 — notably higher than the €10–12 figure many older guides still repeat; no Belém Tower combo ticket found on the current official page.

Summer (Mar 1–Oct 31) daily 09:00–21:00 (last admission 20:30); winter daily 09:00–18:00 (last admission 17:30); closed only 5 days/year (Jan 1, May 1, Dec 24/25/31). Adult admission €17; advance ticket not mandatory.
Onboard cash single tram fare €3.30; Navegante zapping pay-per-use €1.72/journey (min top-up €3); 24h Carris+Metro pass €7.25. A 24h pass breaks even after ~3 tram rides.

Praça do Comércio (locally 'Terreiro do Paço') is one of the largest squares in Europe, on the site of the former royal palace destroyed in the 1755 earthquake; features Pátio da Galé, Cais das Colunas, Arco da Rua Augusta, and an equestrian statue of King José I.

Wed–Mon 10:00–19:00, closed Tuesdays (and Jan 1, May 1, Dec 25). Portugal-resident €12 / non-resident €16 (single ticket covers MAAT Central + Gallery); students under 30 get 25% off, seniors 65+ get 15% off.

LX Factory is a former 1846 textile/printing complex in Alcântara under the 25 de Abril bridge, repurposed since 2008 into shops/studios/restaurants/street art; no confirmed official general opening hours exist (the official site returned unreadable content) — individual shops/restaurants keep their own hours, so it functions as an always-browsable outdoor complex rather than a ticketed venue with fixed hours.

Park 09:00–19:00 (last entry 18:00); Palace 09:30–18:30 (last ticket 17:30, last admission 18:00). Park-only adult €12; Palace+Park ('Essential Visit') adult €20. Palace interior requires a mandatory pre-booked timed-entry slot, no delay tolerance.

Parques de Sintra properties (Pena Palace included) are open every day of the year except Dec 24, 25, 31 and Jan 1, plus rare extraordinary closures (fire risk, extreme weather, state events) — the widely-repeated third-party claim that Pena Palace 'closes Tuesdays' plus Easter/May 1/Jun 13 is NOT supported by the official site and is aggregator misinformation.

Jan–Mar & Oct–Dec 10:00–18:30, Apr–Sep 09:00–19:30 (last entrance 17:30 year-round). Adult admission €20, prices explicitly valid from Jan 2026 — treat any pre-2026 published price as outdated. Closed Jan 1, Dec 24/25/31.
09:30–18:00, last ticket/admission 17:30; ticket office closed 12:00–13:00 (vending machines available). Adult admission €12.

Park 09:00–19:00 (last admission 18:00); Palace 09:30–18:00 (last admission 17:30). Adult admission €12. Roof/scaffolding restoration is underway 'until the first quarter of 2027' — the palace stays open throughout but the hop-on-hop-off electric shuttle is currently suspended; since the trip is Apr 2027 (Q2), scaffolding is officially slated to be gone by then, but restoration timelines commonly slip.

Sintra monuments (Pena, Moorish Castle, Monserrate, Capuchos) have twice been closed for several days on short notice in summer (Aug 2025, Jul 2026) due to extreme heat/wildfire risk alerts. This is a Jun–Sep risk pattern, not something that has historically hit April — the Apr 10–19, 2027 window is lower-risk but not zero-risk. Check parquesdesintra.pt/en/notices/ before departure.
Open daily 09:00–19:30.

Ticket tiers repeated consistently across multiple booking/aggregator sites: Silver €10 (redeemable against a book purchase), Gold €15.95 (incl. a Livraria Lello Editions book), Platinum ≈€50 (rare/first-editions room access) — but the official booking domain (tickets.livrarialello.pt) is a JS-rendered SPA that would not yield pricing content to automated fetch across two attempts. Treat these figures as consistent-but-unconfirmed; Lello is known to adjust ticket tiers periodically.
Daily 09:00–19:00 (extended to 23:00 during Easter/Summer/Christmas); last entry 30 min before closing. Day ticket adult €10, students €7 (ID required); combo tower+Stock Exchange Palace+MMIPO €25.

Summer 09:00–18:30, winter 09:00–17:30, closed Christmas and Easter; Sunday/weekday Mass at 11:00. Cloister/museum admission ≈€4 (aggregator-sourced only — the diocese's own fetched page didn't show a price).

Two-level iron bridge across the Douro; upper deck carries pedestrians + Porto Metro Line D, lower deck carries pedestrians + vehicles. Free to walk on both decks, no ticket, open-air public infrastructure with no fixed hours.

Functioning CP passenger station whose main hall is decorated with ~22,000 azulejo tiles depicting Portuguese history; free to view as a public station concourse. Named 7th most beautiful railway station in Europe by European Best Destinations, Jan 2024.

Ribeira is Porto's UNESCO World Heritage riverside historic district. The correct official municipal tourism citation is visitporto.travel (confirmed via its own footer to be run by Porto City Council / Câmara Municipal do Porto) — NOT porto.travel, a well-produced but privately-run ('Guiajando') lookalike site that ranks prominently in search and is sometimes mistaken for the official source.
Porto Sandeman Visit €23 (50 min, 3 wines); Sandeman 1790 Visit €35 (1h30, 5 wines); Wine & Chocolate Experience €32 (1h, 3 wines + chocolate); Old Tawnies Visit €53 (1h30, 4 wines).
Cellar hours 10:00–18:15 daily (holiday exceptions); Tasting Room 10:00–19:30 daily. Audio-guided self-tour in 13 languages includes 3 wines; base tour price not shown on the fetched page.

Porto.CARD has been temporarily unavailable for purchase since early Jul 2026 due to a stated 'product restructuring process,' with no announced relaunch date as of Aug 2026. Last confirmed 2026 pricing: 24h €7.50, 48h €12, 72h €16, 96h €18; does NOT include public transport. This must be re-checked close to the Apr 2027 trip.

Lisboa Card (valid pricing 1 Apr 2026–31 Mar 2027): 24h adult €31, 48h €51, 72h €62 (online promo shown as €58.90 for 72h). Covers free Metro/Carris/CP(Sintra & Cascais lines)/Fertagus travel and free entry to ~50–52 museums/monuments incl. Jerónimos, Belém Tower, São Jorge Castle. A lookalike reseller domain (lisboacard.org, via ticketbar.eu) brands itself 'The Official Lisbon Pass' but is a third-party reseller, not the issuer — the genuine issuer is shop.visitlisboa.com (Turismo de Lisboa).

A commonly repeated claim (US State Dept–sourced per aggregator mentions) says Tram 28 is notorious for pickpocketing, advising against standing near doors — but direct fetches of both travel.state.gov (403) and osac.gov (405) failed, so this could not be corroborated against a primary government source in this pass. Treat as an unverified-but-widely-repeated caution, not a confirmed official warning.

Pena Palace is calmest in the first entry slots after opening; crowds build steadily through mid-morning and stay heavy into mid-afternoon (roughly 10:30-15:00) as day-trip trains, tour buses, and cruise excursions converge, then thin out again after about 16:00.

Adult (18-64) tickets at Park and National Palace of Pena: Park-only €12; combined Park + Palace ('Essential visit') €20. Park opens 09:00-19:00 (last admission 18:00); Palace interior 09:30-18:30 (last admission ~17:30-18:00). Palace interior entry uses a timed booking slot.

Monserrate draws noticeably fewer visitors than Pena Palace or Quinta da Regaleira — even in peak season it's realistic to have palace rooms and much of the garden largely to yourself, in sharp contrast to a crowded morning at those two.

Combined Park + Palace of Monserrate adult ticket (18-64): €12. Park 09:00-19:00 (last admission 18:00); Palace 09:30-18:00 (last admission 17:00-17:30).
Convent of the Capuchos adult ticket (18-64): €11. Open 09:00-17:30, last admission 17:00.

Leaving Lisbon for Sintra before about 09:00, rather than mid-morning, reaches the main sights well ahead of the day-tripper wave — crowds build steadily through mid-morning and stay heavy until about 16:00, so an early train (and letting one packed bus 434 pass rather than boarding standing-room-only) pays off.

CP's Alfa Pendular Lisbon-Porto service sells 'Promo' fares (bookable 5-60 days ahead, discounted, non-refundable) alongside refundable 'Normal' fares in 1st/2nd class; seats are assigned by carriage/number (ID required at boarding), and luggage rides with you — a small overhead rack per seat plus a shared rack near each carriage entrance, no separate baggage car.

Restaurants directly on the Cais da Ribeira promenade are consistently identified by Porto-based food writers as the city's clearest tourist-trap cluster — laminated photo menus, street touts, and inflated prices are the norm; walking two streets back (toward Clérigos, the Cathedral, or Bonfim) reaches genuinely local kitchens at lower prices.

Ribeira is 'a tourist area par excellence, so it has plenty of tourist traps' — most restaurants there are 'all icing, no cake, and expensive too'; the genuinely good venues (traditional Portuguese, seafood, fine dining) sit just off the promenade, not on it.

Bufete Fase is a small, cash-only lunch counter off the tourist path — a distinct broth-based francesinha sauce (lighter on tomato, built on a secret meat broth) served to a crowd of regulars and office workers rather than tour groups, in contrast to Café Santiago's queues down the street.

Pastéis de Belém draws real queues and heavy foot traffic, but the line visible outside is almost always for takeaway only — walking in through the main entrance reaches a 1,000+ seat dine-in room most visitors never realize exists, with a table usually available in under 10 minutes even at peak times. Quietest before 09:00 on weekdays or after 18:00 any day; peak congestion is 10:00–17:00, especially weekends Apr–Oct.

Manteigaria (Chiado) and Pastéis de Belém are close enough in quality that queue length, tourist density, and travel time matter more than the taste difference; Manteigaria has no real line and sits centrally, while Belém is worth the trip mainly if already visiting the monastery.

disagreements.topic: Whether Pena Palace closes on Tuesdays (plus Easter/May 1/Jun 13), as widely repeated by third-party aggregator sites, versus the official Parques de Sintra position that its properties are open every day except Dec 24/25/31 and Jan 1.
disagreements.investigation: Fetched the official Parques de Sintra FAQ page directly, which states explicitly that properties are open year-round except the four named December/January dates, plus rare extraordinary closures (fire risk, weather, state events).
disagreements.resolution: The official FAQ wins — Pena Palace does NOT close on Tuesdays. The 'closed Tuesdays' claim is aggregator misinformation and must not be repeated in the guide or used to schedule the Sintra day.

disagreements.topic: Multiple third-party booking sites (Viator, Busbud, TripAdvisor) still list the Aerobus airport shuttle as bookable, while the official Lisbon Airport transport page omits it entirely and aerobus.pt 404s.
disagreements.investigation: Fetched the official Lisbon Airport transport page directly (lists Metro, Carris buses, FlixBus, taxi — no Aerobus); attempted aerobus.pt directly (404); cross-checked via a TripAdvisor forum thread discussing the 2022 cancellation.
disagreements.resolution: Aerobus is discontinued (since 2022). The guide recommends the Metro red line or taxi/rideshare instead, and should not repeat Aerobus fare figures still circulating on booking sites.

disagreements.topic: Most guides (and much aggregator content) still cite 'Scotturb 403' as the bus to Cabo da Roca; Carris Metropolitana took over Sintra-area routes in Jan 2023.
disagreements.investigation: Searched for the current operator/route number; found Carris Metropolitana line 1253 described as the current Sintra↔Cabo da Roca circuit, though the operator's own route page is JS-rendered and could not be fetched for schedule detail.
disagreements.resolution: If a future pass adds Cabo da Roca to the itinerary, cite Carris Metropolitana 1253, not Scotturb 403. Not itinerary-critical this pass since Cabo da Roca was rejected as a candidate for time-budget reasons.

disagreements.topic: The official Jerónimos Monastery page shows €18 adult admission; many older/generic travel guides still quote €10–12.
disagreements.investigation: Fetched the official museusemonumentos.pt ticket page directly (twice, to confirm) — €18 is the current, clearly stated figure.
disagreements.resolution: Ship €18 as the current price; note it's higher than what older guides say so the traveler isn't surprised.

disagreements.topic: Whether ETIAS will be required by the Apr 10–19, 2027 trip. The EU's own site removed its Q4-2026 target in Jul 2026; press/immigration-law commentary now says 2027 is 'most likely' but unconfirmed.
disagreements.investigation: Fetched the official europa.eu entry-rules page (silent on ETIAS); could not get readable content from the official ETIAS SPA site directly; cross-checked via an immigration-law firm's public commentary (Fragomen) and general press.
disagreements.resolution: Not itinerary-changing — ETIAS is very unlikely to be enforced by this trip given no confirmed 2027 date exists yet, but the guide should carry an explicit re-check reminder in the pre-departure checklist rather than assert either way as settled.

transport.notApplicableReason: no route in this itinerary reaches risk R3+ — Lisbon-Porto Alfa Pendular and the Sintra CP line + Scotturb 434/435 buses all run multiple times daily with taxi/Uber as an easy, well-documented fallback if one departure is missed; nothing here is a single-point-of-failure connection

saturation.note: Pass A ran five entity-batched sweeps (entry/money/transit backbone, Lisbon sights, Sintra day trip, Porto sights, food across both cities); Pass B ran ~35 native-first and English searches/fetches across Lisbon/Porto neighborhood dining, Sintra crowd timing, transit reality, and resident phrases. Reconciliation found both passes' late-stage searches converging on the same handful of names, blocked sources, or already-known gaps (JS-rendered cp.pt, Graham's 403, ETIAS's unconfirmed date, reddit.com/tripadvisor.com/fodors.com/lisboasecreta.co/evasoes.pt/tickets.livrarialello.pt blocked) rather than surfacing new serious candidates — a clear duplicate/blocked plateau across both passes combined. Remaining unknowns (exact CP fares, Lello's exact ticket tiers, ETIAS's eventual launch date, the Portugal travel advisory level, Bufete Fase's single-source corroboration gap) are pre-trip recheck items and a networked-pass follow-up, not undiscovered candidates that would change which venues/sights ship.

nativeLanguage.why: No src/data/destinations/portugal.json exists yet for this guide, so language was inferred from the destination (Portuguese) rather than read from a t0Domains list. English-only queries for Lisbon/Porto dining return the same tourist top-10 and SEO listicles every time; Portuguese-language queries (onde comer, tascas, evitar turistas, bairro Anjos/Arroios, gírias portuguesas) and Spanish-language queries for Sintra (the next-best-indexed Romance-language traveler community after Portuguese) surfaced neighborhood-specific finds and local press coverage that pure English search missed entirely.
searchClasses: Portuguese-language restaurant/neighborhood queries (onde comer em Lisboa/Porto, tascas, bairros Anjos/Arroios/Bonfim)
Portuguese-language crowd/experience queries (Time Out Market, Castelo de São Jorge, Cabo da Roca, Livraria Lello)
Portuguese-language food-comparison queries (Manteigaria vs Pastéis de Belém, francesinha)
Portuguese-language slang/phrase queries (expressões e gírias portuguesas)
Spanish-language Sintra palace-comparison queries (Monserrate vs Pena vs Regaleira)
nativeLanguage.yield: Surfaced Lisbon's Arroios/Anjos neighborhood-tasca wave (Visão press coverage, a search-preview-only Lisboa Secreta lead), the Ribeira/Rua Augusta tourist-trap warning repeated across Portuguese travel press and two independent Porto food bloggers, and the Café Santiago vs Bufete Fase local/tourist split. Native-language reddit/forum threads (r/portugal, r/Lisbon) could not be fetched directly — WebFetch blocks reddit.com outright — so those stayed leads-only via search snippets rather than fetched, citable sources; several other native/local pages (lisboasecreta.co, evasoes.pt, tripadvisor.com, fodors.com) returned 403s and were marked blocked rather than promoted to citations. yt-dlp was not available in this environment, so the usual YouTube-transcript social/video aide was skipped per the tool-missing doctrine — no video/social leads were pursued this pass.
